summary: Defines extensions to BGP Link State (BGP-LS) for carrying Seamless Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (S-BFD) information. S-BFD is a simplified way to monitor paths between nodes, and IS-IS and OSPF were already extended to advertise S-BFD details. This document lets that information also be collected through BGP-LS by controllers and other consumers. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Routers keep a shared map of the roads and checks to see if roads still work. This lets that map also include the quick-check helpers, so a controller can see who can run those checks.

questions: how does bgp-ls advertise s-bfd information
what is s-bfd in bgp link state
how does s-bfd work across igp domains
subtitle: A new BGP-LS attribute that lets controllers learn each node's S-BFD discriminators across IGP domains.

tldr.problem: A node that wants to monitor a path end to end with S-BFD must know the discriminator of the far end, but IS-IS and OSPF only advertise it within their own area, level or domain.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9247 defines a BGP-LS Attribute TLV, the S-BFD Discriminators TLV (type 1032), attached to a Node NLRI. It carries 4-octet discriminators copied from the IGP advertisements.
tldr.outcome: Discriminators can be distributed through BGP-LS across IGP domains and even across multiple Autonomous Systems within an administrative domain.

facts.label: Attached to
facts.value: BGP-LS Attribute of the Node NLRI

today: RFC 9247 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2022, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Problem This Solves
sections.content:
Seamless BFD (S-BFD, RFC 7880) is a simplified way to use Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (RFC 5880) with large parts of the negotiation removed. It brings quick provisioning and more control and flexibility to nodes that start path monitoring.

To monitor a service path end to end, the head-end node (the Initiator) needs the S-BFD Discriminator of the tail-end node (the Responder). IS-IS (RFC 7883) and OSPF (RFC 7884) already advertise these, so an Initiator learns them for Responders in its IGP area or level, or optionally its domain.

Networks are often split into several IGP domains for scaling and operations, and the endpoints often sit in different domains. This document extends BGP-LS to carry the discriminators further.
sections.eli5: To check that a friend far away is still awake, you need to know their special knock. Until now you could only learn the knocks of people on your own street.

sections.title: BGP-LS as the Carrier
sections.content:
BGP Link State (BGP-LS, RFC 7752) collects and distributes IGP link-state topology information over BGP sessions, across IGP areas, levels and domains. A node's S-BFD discriminators can therefore travel with the topology information across IGP domains and across multiple Autonomous Systems within one administrative domain.

BGP-LS already has a Node NLRI for advertising nodes, with their attributes carried in the BGP-LS Attribute. The S-BFD discriminators are treated as a node-level attribute and advertised that way.
sections.eli5: BGP-LS is like a big shared map that many neighborhoods contribute to. Putting the knocks on that map makes them visible everywhere.

sections.title: The S-BFD Discriminators TLV
sections.content:
The new BGP-LS Attribute TLV is the S-BFD Discriminators TLV. It has a Type field of 1032, a Length field, and one or more discriminators.

Length is variable. It MUST be at least 4 octets and grows by 4 octets for each additional discriminator. Each discriminator is 4 octets and holds a local S-BFD discriminator value of the node. At least one discriminator MUST be included.
sections.eli5: It is a small labeled box. The label says what is inside, a number says how big the box is, and then come the knocks, one after another.

sections.title: Where the Values Come From
sections.content:
The TLV can be added to the BGP-LS Attribute associated with the Node NLRI that originates the corresponding IGP TLV or sub-TLV. The information is derived from the IGP advertisements:

  • IS-IS: the S-BFD Discriminators sub-TLV defined in RFC 7883.
  • OSPFv2 and OSPFv3: the S-BFD Discriminator TLV defined in RFC 7884.

BGP-LS does not invent the values. It copies information that the IGPs already advertise.
sections.eli5: The map maker does not make up the knocks. It copies them from what each neighborhood already announced.

sections.title: IANA Allocation and Manageability
sections.content:
IANA has permanently allocated code point 1032, named S-BFD Discriminators, in the registry of BGP-LS Node Descriptor, Link Descriptor, Prefix Descriptor, and Attribute TLVs. The registry column for the IS-IS TLV or sub-TLV should be left empty.

On manageability, the extension adds to the IGP topology information already distributed through BGP-LS and does not affect BGP operations and management beyond what RFC 7752 already discusses. The malformed-attribute tests in its Fault Management section now also cover the new TLV.
sections.eli5: The new label got an official number in the public list, and the usual rules for spotting broken labels now cover it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension does not change the BGP security model beyond RFC 7752, which calls for limiting the nodes and consumers that receive BGP-LS topology information to trusted entities within an administrative domain. The IGP instances originating the information are assumed to provide any required security and authentication, as described in RFC 7883 and RFC 7884.

One new risk is stated plainly. Advertising discriminators through BGP-LS makes it possible for attackers to initiate S-BFD sessions using them. The vulnerabilities and mitigations are discussed in RFC 7880.
sections.eli5: Sharing the knocks widely means a stranger who sees the map could knock too. So the map should only be shown to trusted people.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: At least 4 octets, plus 4 for each additional discriminator.

fields.name: Discriminator 1
fields.desc: A local S-BFD discriminator of the node. At least one is required.
